name: BroadcastAuthorizationSpec
source_title: BroadcastAuthorization CrySL rule source — canonical requested location was attempted but no rule content was available
important_note: This is a provisional detector-semantics description, not a verified CrySL protocol. The requested canonical BroadcastAuthorization.crysl location was attempted but did not yield usable rule content, and no primary rule definition was established. android.content.BroadcastAuthorization is therefore a convention-required symbolic model type, not an established Android SDK class.

events.name: receive_control_broadcast
events.condition: Observed when a BroadcastReceiver.onReceive implementation reads an Intent action and compares it with either FTP-control action. This observation does not satisfy authorization: that predicate requires evidence that the effective receiver registration or manifest declaration permits external delivery and that an applicable sender restriction does not exclude the asserted sender.

events.name: start_ftp_service
events.condition: Observed when the receiver constructs an explicit FtpService Intent and calls startService. The runtime start predicate requires delivery of an incoming broadcast whose action equals ACTION_START_FTPSERVER, FtpService.isRunning() evaluates false, execution reaches the call, and the operation is not blocked or fails.

events.name: stop_ftp_service
events.condition: Observed when the receiver constructs an explicit FtpService Intent and calls stopService. The runtime stop predicate requires delivery of an incoming broadcast whose action equals ACTION_STOP_FTPSERVER and execution reaches the call without preventing failure.

events.name: require_sender_authorization
events.condition: For dynamically registered receivers, observing a registerReceiver overload is not proof of authorization. The predicate requires either a non-exported registration appropriate to the required broadcasts, or a non-null sender permission whose effective grant semantics exclude the asserted attacker. For manifest receivers, equivalent evidence is outside callback source: the effective merged manifest receiver exported and permission attributes, plus any application-level inherited permission.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that android.content.BroadcastAuthorization is a real Android framework type; no Android SDK declaration for that class was established.
Do not infer the exact CrySL event language, constraints, predicates, or error message because BroadcastAuthorization.crysl was not retrieved.
Do not infer that an onReceive method is externally invocable solely because it compares a custom Intent action.

Do not infer broadcast delivery from a source-level match; delivery depends on the installed APK's effective manifest or dynamic-registration state, Android version, action matching, and platform policy.
Do not infer that startService or stopService actually executes merely because a matching branch appears in source.
Do not infer that the receiver has no protection without inspecting the effective merged manifest and any dynamically applied checks.
Do not infer signature-level authorization from the existence of a custom permission.

Do not equate a dangerous custom permission with a signature permission: signature permissions are limited to apps sharing the declaring app's signing certificate, whereas dangerous permissions have different grant semantics.
Do not infer exploitation, remote reachability, impact, or CVE applicability from this normalized advisory finding alone.
Do not infer that the v3.4.2 tagged fix used a signature-level permission: its tagged AndroidManifest.xml declares CONTROL_FTP_SERVER with protectionLevel="dangerous".
semantic_scope: The apparent rule family concerns Android broadcast authorization at a receiver-to-privileged-action boundary. For the reported Amaze File Manager v3.4.1 example, the source-level observable is FtpReceiver.onReceive selecting two FtpService control actions and invoking Context.startService or Context.stopService. The security-relevant configuration predicate is primarily manifest-level rather than an API-call-ordering property.

detector_semantics.claim: The normalized finding asserts a potential externally controllable FTP-service start/stop path through com.amaze.filemanager.asynchronous.services.ftp.FtpReceiver.onReceive in source tag v3.4.1, paired with an assertion that sufficient sender authorization was absent.
predicates: A receiver implementation consumes an incoming Intent action.
The action is one of the FTP server start or stop control actions.
The corresponding branch invokes Context.startService or Context.stopService for FtpService.
The receiver is externally reachable under the effective component configuration.
No applicable sender-side restriction, such as a required permission or a non-exported component boundary, prevents the claimed external sender.
limitations: The canonical BroadcastAuthorization CrySL rule was not available, so the exact detector predicate set is unknown.
The finding message is an advisory-normalized record rather than a runtime trace.
Static source matching cannot establish installed-manifest merging, permission grants, broadcast delivery, branch feasibility, service-start success, or attacker identity.

The representative v3.4.1 source confirms the action checks and service calls, while its manifest is reported to confirm an exported receiver with no receiver permission at that tag; this does not itself prove a runtime exploit in a particular build or device configuration.

documented_behavior: Android manifest receivers can be exposed to broadcasts from other applications with android:exported="true".
A receiver-level android:permission restricts senders to those holding that permission.
Dynamic registration can require a broadcaster permission through Context.registerReceiver overloads, or use RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED to block broadcasts from other apps.
The reported v3.4.1 FtpReceiver source compares the incoming action to FtpService.ACTION_START_FTPSERVER and ACTION_STOP_FTPSERVER, then starts or stops an explicit FtpService Intent.
preconditions: A broadcast must match the receiver's registration or manifest intent filter and be delivered by Android.
The effective receiver declaration or registration must allow the sender.
For the start branch, the action must equal ACTION_START_FTPSERVER and FtpService.isRunning() must be false.
For the stop branch, the action must equal ACTION_STOP_FTPSERVER.
The service operation must remain permitted by the installed application's effective configuration and the device's Android-version restrictions.
unknowns: Whether the intended BroadcastAuthorizationSpec models only manifest-declared receivers, dynamically registered receivers, or both.
Whether the intended rule accepts any permission, requires a signature-level permission, requires a protected system broadcast, or accepts a non-exported receiver as an alternative.
Whether the target application used product flavors, manifest merging, or build-time substitutions that alter the effective receiver configuration.
Whether Android-version-specific background-service restrictions affect the practical result of the startService call.

security_semantics.detector_claim: The representative record characterizes v3.4.1 as exposing an FTP-control receiver and service without the asserted authorization control, allowing external broadcast actions to select start or stop behavior.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: The reported v3.4.1 tagged manifest declares FtpReceiver as exported and lists its two FTP-control actions without a receiver permission; its FtpReceiver.onReceive implementation maps matching actions to FtpService start or stop calls. The reported v3.4.2 tagged manifest adds CONTROL_FTP_SERVER to both receiver and service, but declares that custom permission as dangerous rather than signature. A historical pull-request description initially proposed signature level, and review discussion changed it to dangerous.

known_false_positive_shapes: The receiver appears in source but is disabled, removed, or non-exported in the effective merged manifest.
A receiver permission is inherited from the application element or supplied by a build flavor not represented in the inspected source file.
The action is protected by Android or is emitted only by a trusted platform component, with evidence not visible to a simple local matcher.
A dynamic receiver is registered with a required broadcaster permission or RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED, but the detector only sees its callback body.
The matched start or stop call is dead code, test-only code, unreachable under real intent values, or guarded by additional authorization logic not recognized by the detector.
The source tag, package, receiver class, action constant, or manifest differs from the installed artifact associated with the reported advisory.
The service call is blocked by platform execution restrictions, so a reachable broadcast does not produce the modeled start/stop effect.
A permission exists but its effective protection level or grant state does not match a simplistic rule assumption.

detector_examples.message: External finding (CVE-2020-35173): onReceive starts or stops FtpService in response to external broadcast actions. The selected version exposes the receiver and service without the signature-level control permission introduced by the fix. Source tag: v3.4.1. This is a normalized advisory record, not a runtime log.
